_note: Newest first. Dates are when the change landed in the development build. Plain wording for people who print, not for developers.

entries.title: Import your own printer settings
entries.text: File › Import printer settings reads the resins you exported from Lychee Slicer (.lyp) or Photon Workshop (.pwsp) and adds each one to your library, calibrated for the matching printer.

entries.title: Creality Halot X1 resins
entries.text: 11 resins for the Halot X1, from the tables Creality publishes.

entries.title: Minimum cavity width
entries.text: Parts of a cavity narrower than 2 mm (you can change it) stay solid, so no thin pocket traps resin you could never wash out.

entries.title: Overlapping parts hollow as one
entries.text: Models made of parts pushed into each other are joined first and then hollowed, so there are no walls inside walls.

entries.title: Round shafts on big scenes too
entries.text: Large support sets used to be drawn with three to eight sides per shaft to save triangles, losing up to 59 % of their section. Every shaft now has 12 sides.

entries.title: Braces end inside their trunks
entries.text: The ends of braces sit inside the trunks they join instead of on their surface.

entries.title: Antialiasing follows you
entries.text: Changing antialiasing no longer marks a slice as out of date; the slice in use takes the setting you have now.

entries.title: Lighter on memory
entries.text: Undo history keeps at most 2 GB of meshes and the shading cache at most 512 MB, emptied when you close a scene.

entries.title: Shortcuts for the four steps
entries.text: Ctrl+1 to Ctrl+4 jump to Prepare, Hollow, Supports and Slice; Ctrl+Tab moves to the next step.

entries.title: Scene settings
entries.text: The view options chip on the 3D view is now called Scene settings, so it does not clash with the View menu.

entries.title: See the printer's real pixels
entries.text: Zoom the layer view far enough and it shows the printer's own pixels, with the grey levels your file format stores, exactly as they are written in the file.

entries.title: A scene panel
entries.text: A panel on the left lists every plate and its objects. Closed it takes no room; open, only what it needs. Export takes the place of Slice once the slice is up to date.

entries.title: Turns land on what they show
entries.text: Turning with keys or the gizmo lands on the tenth of a degree shown in the panel (15° with Ctrl, 1° with Ctrl+Shift), so −37.0° really is −37.0°.

entries.title: Resin counted from the layers
entries.text: The resin estimate counts the lit pixels of every layer, so parts that overlap are not counted twice. A large model went from 388.5 ml to 329.9 ml, matching UVtools on the same file.

entries.title: Nothing selected in Slice
entries.text: The Slice tab does not select models; your selection comes back when you leave it.

entries.title: Line raft by default, on smaller feet
entries.text: The line raft is the default, and roots on any raft stand on small feet instead of wide discs, so rafts take less room: 18 to 24 copies of one miniature on a plate.

entries.title: Checkboxes on the first click
entries.text: Checkboxes sometimes needed a second click. One is enough now.

entries.title: One raft for all
entries.text: A checkbox puts every set of supports on a plate on a single line raft, so Arrange and Fill pack the models instead of their rafts. Generate never moves anything; a clash is reported with an offer to Arrange all.

entries.title: See the support you are editing
entries.text: Each support preset is shown as a live drawing, in 3D or as a section to scale, with close-ups of the tip and foot. Every dimension on the drawing is a field you can type or drag.

entries.title: Copies share their supports
entries.text: Identical copies standing the same way get their supports computed once: 128 copies went from 1,028 s to 1.5 s. A 106-copy project opens with 260 MB of memory instead of 2.5 GB.

entries.title: Your own support sizes
entries.text: The Supports tab has an Auto page (the three presets) and a Manual page with your own tip sizes for the hand tools. Presets and sizes can be exported and imported.

entries.title: Arrange again is instant
entries.text: Shapes are prepared in the background while the scene is still, and pressing Arrange again with nothing changed answers at once.

entries.title: Arrange all adds plates
entries.text: Whatever does not fit goes to new plates, and plates left empty are removed. Models you placed by hand can stay where they are. Imports go to the first plate with room.

entries.title: Duplicate a plate, Alt-drag a copy
entries.text: Shift and + duplicates the active plate with its models; holding Alt while dragging moves a copy.

entries.title: Slice and export one plate or all
entries.text: Each plate is sliced, reviewed and exported on its own and keeps its own slice; Export all plates writes one file per plate.

entries.title: Several plates in one scene
entries.text: Up to 32 plates, in rows of four, with one undo history and one project. Add, remove and rename them on the plate itself, and drag models between them.

entries.title: Islands painted on the model
entries.text: Islands found by Analyze islands are painted on the model, visible through anything in front of them, and Go to island takes the camera there from below.

entries.title: Where the engine would put tips
entries.text: With Add or Move tip active, green rings show where Generate would place the tips that are still missing.

entries.title: Analyze islands from the Supports tab
entries.text: An Islands card finds every island and offers to support them all, without leaving the tab.

entries.title: Supports stay in step
entries.text: After a repair or a small change, out-of-date supports are redrawn on their own when they still fit, instead of asking you to regenerate.

entries.title: Pre-supported files, all at once
entries.text: Several pre-supported files imported together get one question, and loose bits of supports are recognised as supports.

entries.title: A scene you can read
entries.text: Models in warm grey, supports in slate, the selection outlined in amber, and everything else dimmed.

entries.title: Rafts follow their setting
entries.text: Changing the raft redraws the rafts of existing supports without regenerating them.

entries.title: Drop many to the plate
entries.text: Drop to plate works on every selected object in one step, and Delete in the Supports tab removes only the selected supports.

entries.title: Plane cut
entries.text: Cut a model with a plane, across all of it or only inside an outline, with handles in the scene. A cut takes about 38 ms and always gives closed pieces.

entries.title: The open .bread library
entries.text: Projects are read and written by the open .bread library: smaller files, and the same bytes every time you save the same scene.

entries.title: Solid areas with a lasso
entries.text: Draw a lasso around what must stay solid; the cavity's wall lands exactly on it.

entries.title: The workshop look
entries.text: A new interface: graphite, compact, numbers in monospace, a light main button, amber only for warnings, and the plate drawn like a technical plan with rulers in millimetres.

entries.title: Tips stay on their own surface
entries.text: Tips no longer jump up to whatever hangs above a candidate point: fewer, better placed tips and less resin in supports.

entries.title: Recognise pre-supported files
entries.text: Importing a model that comes with supports offers to keep it as it is, separate the supports, or replace them with Breadslicer's.

entries.title: Step through layers with the keyboard
entries.text: In Slice, up and down move one layer, holding moves five per second (twenty with Shift), and Home and End go to the first and last.

entries.title: A cleaner overhang map
entries.text: On finely detailed models the map reads the surface around each point, so textured tops no longer show red specks.

entries.title: Supports as dotted lines from below
entries.text: Optional: under the plate, supports turn into dotted lines with a ball at each contact.

entries.title: Tips where you click on fine meshes
entries.text: On models with triangles smaller than a pixel, Add reads the surface around the cursor, so it stops refusing real overhangs.

entries.title: Three presets by model size
entries.text: Three support presets: Miniatures (20–65 mm), Figures (65–150 mm) and Statues (150 mm and up).

entries.title: The map knows where your tips are
entries.text: The overhang map shows in Prepare, Supports and Slice, and fades where a support tip already holds the surface.

entries.title: A pillar grid you can set
entries.text: Zone presets can turn the pillar grid on or off and set its spacing.

entries.title: Under the plate
entries.text: With the camera below the plate, the plate and the raft fade away, and the tools pick the supports behind them.

entries.title: A new support structure
entries.text: Pillars on a grid spread the peel force over the plate, tips end in a sphere on the exact point, tall trunks get braces, and islands hang small supports from the nearest support.

entries.title: Repair keeps your supports
entries.text: Repairing a model redraws its supports on the repaired mesh when every tip still fits, instead of leaving them out of date.

entries.title: The review in one sweep
entries.text: The review reads every layer once: 58 s to 0.65 s on a large hollow model. Fix all: 868 s to about 3 s, in one undo step.

entries.title: Add supports? after slicing
entries.text: If a slice finds islands, a card asks whether to add the missing tips, and places them where they really hold the island.

entries.title: Hollows are never filled
entries.text: Only sealed pockets smaller than 1 ml are ever filled. Suction cups and larger cavities ask for drains, and a hollow made in Breadslicer is never filled.

entries.title: Big 3MF files save safely
entries.text: Large sliced 3MF files are written in parts to a temporary file, so saving can no longer run out of memory or damage the previous file.

entries.title: The layer view opens
entries.text: The layer view panel opens next to the 3D view and zooms towards the cursor.

entries.title: G from the top view stays flat
entries.text: Moving with G from an aligned view no longer nudges the model up or down.

entries.title: Protect detail
entries.text: Paint surfaces in Orient with the Protect detail brush, and auto-orient keeps support tips off them.

entries.title: Live overhang map
entries.text: The model is painted red where it needs support while you turn it, at no measurable cost.

entries.title: Open files into the running app
entries.text: Launch Breadslicer with several model files and they arrive in one scene, each with its file name. With the app already open, new files go to the window you used last instead of starting a second copy.

entries.title: Copy and paste keeps your prep
entries.text: A pasted object brings its hollow and drains, its own editable supports with your hand edits, and its height. One undo takes it all back.

entries.title: Add braces by hand
entries.text: A new Brace tool (C) joins two supports with two clicks, with a green or red preview that says why. Remove takes out a single brace, and every brace is one undo.

entries.title: World and model size side by side
entries.text: When a model is tilted, the Size card shows its size in the world next to its own size. Both can be edited.

entries.title: The first click on an imported model is instant
entries.text: Everything needed to pick a model with the mouse is now prepared while the file loads, so the first click no longer stalls on big miniatures.

entries.title: The start screen comes back on an empty scene
entries.text: Delete the last object or close the scene and the start screen returns, with your recent files. Ctrl+Z brings everything back.

entries.title: Fix all works in the background
entries.text: Fix all no longer freezes the window on scenes with hundreds of findings. It shows its progress and can be cancelled; the result is the same as before.

entries.title: A repair report you can read
entries.text: The Repair report opens with every detail shown, in larger text, and the card grows to fit what it says.

entries.title: Importing several files at once
entries.text: Drop four models and they arrive together, read in parallel, instead of one first and the rest a second later.

entries.title: Generate supports for every selected model
entries.text: With several models selected, Generate makes one set per model, with progress, in a single undo step. A new option lifts models that sit on the plate by 5 mm first.

entries.title: Import adds to the scene
entries.text: File › Import model (Ctrl+I), drag and drop, and the start screen now add models to the current scene, placed in free space without moving anything. Opening a .bread project still replaces the scene.

entries.title: New message cards
entries.text: Every message card now shares the start screen's look: a clear header, a close button and the buttons in the footer.

entries.title: Manual supports: move tips, remove many at once
entries.text: A new Move tip tool (M) drags a support's tip across the surface with a live green or red preview. Remove now works with a box or a brush, and only touches supports you can actually see.

entries.title: A start screen
entries.text: Reopen your last project, open a project, import a model or start empty, with your 10 recent files. It can be turned off in Preferences.

entries.title: Manual supports that attach where you click
entries.text: A hand-placed support hooks onto nearby trunks, Shift+click forces one, keys 1 to 4 pick the tip size, and the preview says why a support cannot attach. A support that needs its own trunk gets bracing to its neighbour.

entries.title: Transform, Supports and Slice in Spanish
entries.text: The rest of the main panels are translated.

entries.title: Filled cavities print without a seam
entries.text: A cavity filled from the review now covers its border pixels too, so no thin line is left where it meets the model.

entries.title: Fill bed
entries.text: Fill the free space of the plate with copies of the selected model, or a fair mix of several. Copies share their mesh, keep their own supports, and the rest of the plate stays where it is.

entries.title: Drains with depth, cones and plugs
entries.text: Drain holes take a fixed or automatic depth, can be cone-shaped, and can come with a matching plug placed next to the model.

entries.title: Presets by model size
entries.text: Two new support presets, for miniatures from 30 mm and figures from 70 mm, size tips, trunks and bracing by zone.

entries.title: Repair shows what it did, and can be cancelled
entries.text: Progress per object, a Cancel that leaves the scene untouched, and red or amber marks on whatever could not be fixed.

entries.title: Paste is instant
entries.text: Pasting a copy of a large model takes about 3 ms, and undoing it about 0.1 ms.

entries.title: Faster start
entries.text: The window appears sooner, on the first launch and on every one after.

entries.title: Closer print time estimates
entries.text: Anycubic printers that use the ZIP file now get a time estimate within a few percent of the real print.

entries.title: Gizmo, second round
entries.text: Plane handles to move on two axes, press and drag any model to move it, a focused gizmo style and a gizmo size setting in Preferences, and R R / S S to turn or scale each selected object around its own centre.

entries.title: A new gizmo
entries.text: Clear outlines and axis colours, live numbers while you drag, a dashed path when moving and a slice when rotating. Ctrl snaps, Shift moves finely.

entries.title: Multi-select
entries.text: Shift+click and Shift+drag a box to select several models. Move, rotate, scale, delete and arrange them together, in one undo step.

entries.title: Orbit around what matters
entries.text: The camera orbits around the selection or the point under the cursor, and the numeric keypad turns the view in 15° steps.

entries.title: Prints on the Photon Mono M7 Pro finish cleanly
entries.text: The Anycubic ZIP file now ends the way the printer expects, so the print no longer stalls on its last layer.

entries.title: Repair that makes broken models printable
entries.text: Repair now welds cracks, separates parts that touch on an edge, orients every piece and closes holes. Every broken model of our test set slices after it.

entries.title: Auto-orient
entries.text: Quick and Full searches for a pose with fewer supports and less peel force, with a live preview and a single undo.

entries.title: The hollow is exactly the preview
entries.text: The cavity you see is the cavity you get: the preview and the result are the same mesh, with the wall measured exactly.

entries.title: Drains cut through infill
entries.text: A drain hole removes every infill pillar or lattice bar it touches, so nothing is left floating inside the channel.

entries.title: Split into bodies
entries.text: Pull a model apart into its separate bodies, or keep only one of them.

entries.title: More files open
entries.text: Duplicate faces are dropped on import, and 3MF files from other tools with untyped parts open.

entries.title: Overlapping parts print
entries.text: Parts that overlap inside one model are no longer dropped from the layers.

entries.title: Resin scale compensation is applied
entries.text: The X/Y/Z compensation in a resin profile now scales the model, its supports and the raft.

entries.title: Files land where you put the model
entries.text: Printer files were rotated half a turn on the plate. Now the model prints where it sits in the app.

entries.title: A much faster viewport
entries.text: The viewport no longer walks every vertex on every frame: a heavy scene went from 55 to 446 frames per second on our machine.

entries.title: Autosave and recovery
entries.text: Unsaved work is kept in the background every 2 minutes and offered back after a crash. Saving over a project keeps its previous versions.

entries.title: Export diagnostics
entries.text: Help › Export Diagnostics saves a .zip you can attach to a bug report, with your user name and folders removed. An optional diagnostic log records the session until you close the app.

entries.title: Arrange all
entries.text: Packs models by their real shape at every height, 1 mm apart, in one undo step.

entries.title: 157 printers
entries.text: The printer list now covers 20 brands, with panels, mirroring and build heights checked against an open-source reference.

entries.title: Supports follow their model
entries.text: Each model has its own supports and raft. Moving or turning a model carries its supports along; tilting or scaling it regenerates them.
